{\em the observed spectra of pulsars can be explained quantitatively in terms of a superluminar emission process that generates a radiation spectrum whose oscillations are determined by the plasma frequency and electron gyrofrequency in a conventional pulsars magnetosphere}.

{\it the entire spectrum of a pulsar can be accounted for in terms of a radiation mechanism that involves the propagation of electromagnetic radiation in a vacuum medium, and that this radiation mechanism can account for the entire spectrum, including the radio, ultraviolet, and X-ray bands}.

the observed spectral intensities of all nine pulsars considered can be explained quantitatively in terms of a superluminous current that is distributed uniformly in a spherical volume of a size that is comparable with the size of a conventional pulsar's magnetosphere, and that rotates with a period that is shorter than the period of the rotation of the neutron star.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the question of whether or not a single emission process, whose spectrum is determined by a few fundamental parameters of the source (in particular, by the rotation rate of the source), can account for all the observed features of the pulsar radiation spectrum.
the development of a unified theory of pulsar radiation, and with the application of that theory to the analysis of observational data.

the possibility that the observed pulsar spectra may be generated by a single emission process that is common to all pulsars, and that is based on the same physical principles as the radiation emitted by a superluminously rotating polarization current in vacuum.

the present model provides a unified description of the emission from a broad range of pulsars, and that the model can be considered as a viable alternative to the standard models of the pulsar magnetosphere.

the present model provides the first {\em quantitative} explanation of the spectra of the entire set of pulsars for which data are available in the frequency range from radio to gamma rays, and that the model is consistent with the notion of the pulsar magnetosphere as a vacuum cavity filled with a plasma whose density is determined by the plasma frequency and electron gyrofrequency.
